papers.title: Selective cytotoxicity of [Cu(theophylline)(H2O)2Cl2] complex toward cancer cells: insights from structural, spectroscopic, and molecular docking analyses.
papers.abstract: The diaquadichlorotheophylline-copper(ii) coordination complex, [Cu(theophylline)(H2O)2Cl2], was synthesized via slow solvent evaporation and comprehensively characterized through experimental and computational approaches. X-ray powder diffraction and Rietveld refinement confirmed a triclinic crystal system (space group P1̄(C 1 i )) with pentacoordinate copper(ii) in a square-pyramidal geometry. Thermal analyses revealed thermal stability up to 358 K, with dehydration requiring 89.5 kJ mol-1 per H2O molecule. Vibrational spectroscopy (Fourier transform infrared and Raman) combined with density
papers.summary: This study characterizes a copper-theophylline complex and shows it selectively kills cancer cells, with molecular docking suggesting a potential mechanism of action. The complex was structurally resolved using X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy, and its thermal properties were determined.

papers.title: Physicochemical developability insights into human Fab fragments with extended hypervariable loops.
papers.abstract: Human antibodies with extended complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) can offer distinctive therapeutic opportunities by enabling binding to difficult targets. However, potential developability issues could pose problems for pharmaceutical development. Here, we used integrated experimental and computational workflows to analyze five human Fabs with a long third CDR in their heavy chains (CDR-H3). We assessed their secretion, homogeneity, conformational stability, colloidal stability, and non-specific binding, and complemented these analyses with molecular dynamics simulations to probe conf
papers.summary: This study investigates the developability of human antibody fragments (Fabs) with extended CDR-H3 loops, which are promising for targeting difficult antigens but may face manufacturing challenges. Using experimental assays and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors assess secretion, stability, and non-specific binding, providing insights into how these long loops affect pharmaceutical properties.

papers.title: Exposure-informed lung transcriptomic analysis links predicted NNK targets to cell type-specific remodeling programs in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is associated with cigarette smoking, yet the relationship between the tobacco-specific nitrosamine nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) and IPF-associated lung transcriptional remodeling remains incompletely understood. Here, we developed an exposure-informed computational framework integrating multi-database target prediction, lung single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic analysis, co-expression network analysis, bulk lung cohort projection, and exploratory structure-based modeling. Putative human protein targets of NNK were predicted from ChEMBL
papers.summary: This study develops a computational framework integrating target prediction, single-cell transcriptomics, and network analysis to link the tobacco-specific nitrosamine NNK to cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). The findings suggest potential NNK targets that may drive IPF-associated gene programs, providing a mechanistic link between smoking and IPF progression.

papers.title: Probing pyrazolo-pyrimidines as SIRT2 inhibitors via molecular modelling and biological assays.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRTs) involvement in different biological pathways opens a promising scenario for the development of related ligands to be evaluated as therapeutic agents in different diseases, such as cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, diabetes, cardiovascular and autoimmune diseases. The continuous elucidation of several SIRT2-ligand complexes fostered the discovery of novel and more selective SIRT2 inhibitors (SIRT2Is). Among them, SIRT2 in the presence of SirReal2 analogues was the most investigated. We recently reported pyrazolo-pyrimidine compounds (1-5) as SIRT2Is (1, SIRT2 % inhibition =
papers.summary: This study investigates pyrazolo-pyrimidine compounds as selective SIRT2 inhibitors using molecular modeling and biological assays, identifying promising leads for therapeutic applications in diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration. The work combines computational docking with experimental validation to characterize binding and inhibitory activity.

papers.title: Behind substrate specificity switch in lactate dehydrogenase: Active-site loop dynamics and epistatic enhancement.
papers.abstract: Substrate specificity in lactate dehydrogenases (LDHs) controls metabolic flux and remains a central challenge in enzyme engineering, particularly when closely related substrates differ by only a single carboxylate group. Although Q102 (equivalent to Gln86 in Geobacillus stearothermophilus L-LDH) is recognized as a canonical substrate-specificity determinant, how this electrostatic switch cooperates with steric effects, conformational dynamics, and scaffold context to govern substrate recognition remains unclear. Here, we combined steady-state kinetics with molecular dynamics simulations to ex
papers.summary: This study investigates how substrate specificity in lactate dehydrogenase is controlled by an active-site loop, revealing that the canonical Q102 electrostatic switch works together with steric effects and conformational dynamics. Using kinetics and molecular dynamics, the authors show that epistatic interactions with the scaffold context enhance the specificity switch, providing insights for enzyme engineering.

papers.title: Quantifying protein unfolding kinetics with a high-throughput microfluidic platform.
papers.abstract: Even after folding, proteins sample unfolded intermediates at risk of irreversible alteration (e.g., via proteolysis, aggregation, or posttranslational modification). Thus, kinetic stability impacts protein lifetime and abundance. However, we have very few measurements of unfolding rates, largely due to technical challenges. To address this, we developed SPARKfold (simultaneous proteolysis assay revealing kinetics of folding), a microfluidic platform to express, purify, and measure unfolding rate constants at high throughput via native proteolysis. We applied SPARKfold to determine unfolding r
papers.summary: The authors developed SPARKfold, a high-throughput microfluidic platform that can express, purify, and measure protein unfolding rate constants via native proteolysis. This addresses the technical challenges that have limited measurements of kinetic stability, which is important for understanding protein lifetime and abundance in cells.

papers.title: Three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction by atomic force microscopy imaging and template matching allows rapid structural-based validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image.
papers.abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) is a versatile multi-modal imaging method frequently used for structural characterisation of biological surfaces at the nanoscale. However, AFM-based three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction has hitherto not been possible due to the tip-sample convolution artifact that distorts AFM images of individual molecules, and the disconnect between two-dimensional AFM images of surface deposited molecules and their three-dimensional structures. Here, three-dimensional single-particle analysis was developed for rapid structure-based validation of protein structures
papers.summary: This paper presents a new method for three-dimensional single-particle reconstruction using atomic force microscopy (AFM) combined with template matching, overcoming the tip-sample convolution artifact that previously limited AFM to 2D imaging. The approach enables rapid structural validation of recombinant SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein from a single topology image, demonstrating its utility for quality control in protein production.

papers.title: Binding Modes of Thalidomide Derivatives in Cereblon-Neosubstrate Complexes Revealed by Molecular Dynamics and Free Energy Calculations.
papers.abstract: Immunomodulatory drugs such as thalidomide and its derivatives act as molecular glues by binding to the E3 ligase substrate receptor cereblon (CRBN) and promoting the selective recruitment and degradation of specific neosubstrates. Despite extensive structural and experimental characterization, the molecular origin of ligand-induced neosubstrate selectivity remains incompletely understood. Here, we present a comparative computational study of ternary CRBN-ligand-neosubstrate complexes involving two biologically relevant neosubstrates, IKZF1 and SALL4, and five thalidomide derivatives displayin
papers.summary: This computational study uses molecular dynamics and free energy calculations to compare how five thalidomide derivatives bind in ternary complexes with the E3 ligase receptor cereblon and two neosubstrates, IKZF1 and SALL4. The findings reveal distinct binding modes and energetic contributions that help explain ligand-induced neosubstrate selectivity, offering insights for designing more selective immunomodulatory drugs.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Aβ42 Dimers with Solid-State NMR Restraints Capture the Key Structural Motifs in Aβ42 Fibrillation Pathways.
papers.abstract: Formation of the β-amyloid (Aβ) plaques is a pathological hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is believed to be a primary cause of dementia in elderly individuals. In the present work, we performed molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on the conformational evolution of Aβ42 dimers in solution and in a membrane-like environment to explore the folding of Aβ42 during fibrillation. Particularly, the MD simulation was steered by experimental internuclear distance restraints obtained using solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) spectroscopy. Our results revealed that several hydrophobic
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations guided by solid-state NMR restraints to investigate the conformational evolution of Aβ42 dimers, key intermediates in Alzheimer's disease amyloid fibrillation. The simulations capture structural motifs that are important for understanding how Aβ42 aggregates, providing insights into the early steps of plaque formation.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics and Free Energy Calculations Predict Binding Mode and Affinity Determinants of Specialized Pro-Resolving Mediators at GPR101.
papers.abstract: GPR101 is an orphan G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) with unusually high constitutive activity and has recently emerged as a target for specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), endogenous lipids that actively terminate inflammation and promote tissue repair. Given the therapeutic relevance of pro-resolution signaling in chronic pain and inflammatory disorders, understanding how SPMs engage GPR101 is of great significance. Although cryo-EM structures suggest an occluded orthosteric cavity, SPMs such as RvD5n‑3 DPA are potent agonists, creating uncertainty about their binding modes. Long-tim
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations and free energy calculations to predict how specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) bind to the orphan GPCR GPR101, which is a target for resolving inflammation. The findings reveal a likely binding mode and key affinity determinants, addressing the uncertainty about how these lipid agonists engage a receptor with an apparently occluded orthosteric cavity.

papers.title: Multivalent ion binding site identification with structure-based deep learning.
papers.abstract: Protein-ion interactions are essential for many cellular processes, including enzymatic catalysis, signaling, and allosteric regulation. However, mapping ion-binding sites experimentally remains labor-intensive and expensive. Here, we present BiteNetI, a structure-based deep learning model that uses 3D convolutional neural networks to simultaneously localize ion-binding centers and predict binding residues for 14 biologically relevant ions. Trained on a carefully curated dataset of over 10,000 high-resolution protein-ion complexes, in which near-identical binding sites are consistently annotat
papers.summary: BiteNetI is a deep learning tool that predicts ion-binding sites and residues in proteins from their 3D structure, covering 14 biologically relevant ions. It was trained on a large curated dataset of protein-ion complexes and offers a fast, cost-effective alternative to experimental mapping of ion-binding sites.

papers.title: Development of the First YTHDC1 Degrader with Improved Antileukemia Activity.
papers.abstract: N6-Methyladenosine (m6A) represents the most prevalent internal RNA modification in eukaryotic mRNA, with YTHDC1 serving as a critical nuclear reader protein implicated in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Although selective inhibitors of YTHDC1 have been reported, whether targeted degradation of YTHDC1 could achieve enhanced therapeutic efficacy remains unexplored. Here, we report the rational design and synthesis of the first PROTAC molecule targeting YTHDC1, termed XY-2, which was developed based on the cocrystal structure of YTHDC1 bound to its known inhibitor. XY-2 efficiently induced proteas
papers.summary: This paper reports the first PROTAC degrader (XY-2) targeting the m6A reader protein YTHDC1, designed from a cocrystal structure with a known inhibitor. XY-2 induces proteasomal degradation of YTHDC1 and shows improved antileukemia activity compared to existing inhibitors, suggesting that targeted degradation may offer a more effective therapeutic strategy for AML.

papers.title: A Ligand-Triggered Receptor Conformation Enables the Design of Selective Agonists for the Dopamine 3 Receptor (D3R) Using a Bitopic Strategy.
papers.abstract: While G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) represent the largest drug target family, designing subtype-selective molecules is still a challenge, especially to distinguish among closely related subtypes. One of the most challenging cases is the distinction between dopamine D2R and D3R, pivotal receptors in motor functions and cognition, and targets of Parkinson's disease treatments, schizophrenia, or substance use disorders. Attempts to design D3R-selective molecules with ligands binding toward the first transmembrane helix (the most sequence-diverse and conformationally flexible segment in GPCR
papers.summary: This study reveals a ligand-triggered conformational change in the dopamine 3 receptor (D3R) that enables the design of highly selective agonists using a bitopic strategy, overcoming the challenge of distinguishing D3R from the closely related D2R. The findings provide a new structural basis for developing subtype-selective GPCR drugs with potential therapeutic applications in Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia, and substance use disorders.

papers.title: [Enhancing the thermostability of Pseudoalteromonas sp. κ-carrageenase through computer-aided rational design].
papers.abstract: κ-carrageenan oligosaccharides hold broad application prospects in the food and pharmaceutical fields due to their excellent bioactivity. κ-carrageenase is a key enzyme for the industrial production of high-value carrageenan oligosaccharides, while the insufficient thermostability limits its application. The objective of this study is to rationally redesign the κ-carrageenase derived from Pseudoalteromonas through a computer-aided strategy, with the aim of constructing and screening enzyme variants exhibiting significantly enhanced thermostability. Discovery Studio 2019 was used for multi-site
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used computer-aided rational design to improve the thermostability of a κ-carrageenase from Pseudoalteromonas, an enzyme important for producing bioactive carrageenan oligosaccharides. By introducing targeted mutations, the authors constructed enzyme variants with significantly enhanced thermostability, addressing a key limitation for industrial applications.

papers.title: Integrating AlphaFold2 with physics-based ensemble docking for high-efficiency nanobody discovery.
papers.abstract: Nanobodies, the single-domain counterparts of traditional antibodies, are approximately one-tenth the size yet retain the ability to bind their target antigens tightly and specifically. A major practical bottleneck in developing functional nanobodies is the panning process required to identify them from the vast immunized cDNA libraries derived from camelids. To overcome this bottleneck, we developed a computational framework that progressed from next-generation sequencing (NGS)-derived candidate nanobody sequences to predicted structures using AlphaFold2, and prioritized nanobodies based on p
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates AlphaFold2 structure prediction with physics-based ensemble docking to prioritize nanobody candidates from NGS-derived sequences, bypassing the time-consuming experimental panning process. The approach successfully identifies functional nanobodies with high efficiency, offering a faster and more cost-effective route to nanobody discovery.

papers.title: Localized Rigidification and Allosteric Modulation Mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Neutralization by Class 3 and Class 4 Antibodies at Atomic Resolution: An Integrated Computational Study of Binding, Dynamics, and Allostery.
papers.abstract: The relentless evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and the emergence of highly antibody-evasive variants underscore the need to decipher the molecular principles that govern antibody neutralization breadth and resilience. In this study, we employ an integrated computational framework combining structural analysis, conformational dynamics, mutational scanning, binding energetics, and allosteric network modeling to dissect the mechanistic signatures of class 3 and class 4 antibodies targeting the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Through comprehensive analysis of antibody-RBD co
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses an integrated computational approach—combining structural analysis, molecular dynamics, mutational scanning, binding energetics, and allosteric network modeling—to dissect how class 3 and class 4 antibodies neutralize the SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD. The study reveals that these antibodies induce localized rigidification and allosteric modulation, providing atomic-level mechanistic insights into neutralization breadth and resilience against evolving variants.

papers.title: Repurposing FDA-Approved Drugs as Nav1.7 Channel Modulators: An Integrated Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.7 is a strongly validated target for the development of novel, non-opioid analgesics due to its genetic link to pain signaling. To accelerate the discovery of safe Nav1.7 modulators, this study outlines an integrated computational pipeline to repurpose FDA-approved drugs. A structurally complete model of the Nav1.7 central pore was generated via homology modeling from a high-resolution cryo-EM structure (PDB: 7W9K) to ensure a physically consistent model suitable for dynamic simulations. We conducted a structure-based virtual screening of 2296 FDA-approved
papers.summary: This study uses a computational pipeline combining homology modeling, virtual screening, and molecular dynamics to repurpose FDA-approved drugs as modulators of the Nav1.7 sodium channel, a validated target for non-opioid pain relief. The approach identified potential drug candidates that may be rapidly repurposed for pain management, offering a faster path to clinical application.

papers.title: ProteinDock: A physics-informed layer to improve protein-protein docking reliability.
papers.abstract: Computational modeling provides geometric insight into protein-protein interactions without requiring the resources of experimentation. However, reliability can be hindered when modeling proteins with distinctive features, such as antibodies, that use flexible, polar-rich loops to bind antigens. We developed ProteinDock , a physics-based tool that can be used in combination with leading modeling programs to improve the reliability of protein-protein docking; this work provides a case study of antibody-antigen interfaces. ProteinDock was layered onto Rosetta for docking unbound experimentally d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ProteinDock is a new physics-informed layer that improves the reliability of protein-protein docking, particularly for challenging cases like antibody-antigen interactions with flexible, polar-rich loops. By integrating with existing tools like Rosetta, it enhances docking accuracy for unbound experimental structures, offering a practical improvement for computational modeling of protein complexes.

papers.title: CovSite : A High-Throughput Blind Covalent Screening Framework for Reactive Site Detection.
papers.abstract: Targeted covalent inhibitors are a powerful, yet underexplored, class of therapeutics, and current computational covalent screeners are constrained in early drug discovery due to the need for prior knowledge of the target site and limited throughput. We present CovSite , a blind covalent screening tool that identifies candidate reactive residues across the entire protein surface, utilizing only the protein structure and electrophile SMILES. CovSite applies a pipeline of four orthogonal physicochemical filters (nucleophile identification, solvent accessibility, environment-dependent deprotonati
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CovSite is a new computational tool for blind covalent drug screening that identifies reactive cysteine residues across entire protein surfaces without prior knowledge of the target site. It uses only the protein structure and electrophile SMILES, applying four orthogonal physicochemical filters to rank candidate sites, enabling high-throughput discovery of covalent binding sites.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology Guided Drug Repurposing and Molecular Modeling Identify Sulfasalazine as a Potential OXA-23 β-Lactamase in Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii has become a major health concern, primarily driven by the dissemination of class D β-lactamases, particularly OXA-23, which compromise the efficacy of last-line β-lactam antibiotics. Drug repurposing combined with structure-based computational approaches provides a promising strategy for accelerating the discovery of novel therapeutic candidates against multidrug-resistant pathogens. This study aimed to identify FDA-approved non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) with potential inhibitory activity against OXA-23 β-lac
papers.summary: This study used network pharmacology and molecular modeling to screen FDA-approved NSAIDs for potential inhibitors of the OXA-23 β-lactamase, which is a key driver of carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii. They identified sulfasalazine as a promising repurposing candidate that may inhibit this resistance enzyme, offering a potential new strategy against multidrug-resistant infections.

papers.title: RNA G-quadruplex structure recognition by chimeric peptides.
papers.abstract: G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical nucleic acids involved in gene regulation and have attracted interest as potential therapeutic targets. However, developing ligands that selectively recognize specific G4 structures remains challenging. Here, we report the rational design of chimeric peptides that combine a de novo selected peptide (Pep11) with a native peptide (Rhau18) derived from the endogenous DHX36 protein. The chimeric peptides bound RNA G4s (rG4s) with nanomolar affinity, representing a 10-fold enhancement over the individual modules, while retaining selectivity for rG4s over DNA G
papers.summary: The study reports the rational design of chimeric peptides that combine a de novo selected peptide with a native peptide from the DHX36 protein, achieving nanomolar affinity for RNA G-quadruplexes with 10-fold enhancement over individual modules while maintaining selectivity. This approach offers a new strategy for developing specific RNA G4 ligands, which are potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Quantum Chemical Insights into Antibiotic Structure-Activity Relationships and Mechanisms of Action: A Review.
papers.abstract: This review examines recent quantum chemical methodologies applied to investigating antibiotic structure and mechanisms of action. The discussion is organised into three sections: (1) enzymatic hydrolysis of the β-lactam ring, (2) interactions of antibiotics with ribosomal subunits and enzyme active sites, and (3) complex formation with metal ions. Each section evaluates how quantum chemical approaches, particularly density functional theory (DFT) and hybrid QM/MM techniques, model molecular processes relevant to antibiotic function, including transition states, electron density analyses, and
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent quantum chemical studies on antibiotics, focusing on how computational methods like DFT and QM/MM reveal details of drug action, including beta-lactam ring hydrolysis, ribosome binding, and metal-ion interactions. It highlights how these approaches provide atomic-level insights into structure-activity relationships and mechanisms, which could aid in designing more effective antibiotics.

papers.title: Multiscale stability analysis of electric-field-based air nanobubbles under varying pH and generation time using experimental and molecular dynamics insights.
papers.abstract: Electric-field-based gas nanobubbles (NBs) generation provides a green, chemical-free, and energy-efficient alternative for different environmental applications such as water treatment; however, despite their unique physicochemical properties, a sustainability-oriented understanding of their stability, optimum operating conditions, and the kinetic pathways governing their interfacial evolution remain largely unresolved. This study presents a comprehensive multiscale investigation of air NBs produced under different generation duration and pH conditions, integrating long-term experimental monit
papers.summary: This study investigates the stability of air nanobubbles generated via electric fields under different pH and generation times, combining long-term experiments with molecular dynamics simulations. It identifies optimal conditions for bubble stability and reveals the kinetic pathways governing their interfacial evolution, providing insights for sustainable water treatment applications.

papers.title: Ligand Design Using Unique Conformations to Preferentially Dock a Specific Site on Collagen-Bound MMP1.
papers.abstract: Precise site-specific ligand design remains a major challenge in structure-based drug discovery. Most existing approaches screen ligands against binding pockets identified from static protein structures obtained by X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy, or AlphaFold predictions. However, protein function is governed by a structure-dynamics-function relationship, and ligand screening that does not account for binding competition across the protein surface or the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent conformational states remains incomplete. Substrate-specific confo
papers.summary: This study presents a ligand design approach that leverages unique protein conformations to achieve site-specific docking on collagen-bound MMP1, addressing the limitations of static structure-based drug discovery. By accounting for the receptor's dynamic, substrate-dependent states and binding competition across the protein surface, the method improves selectivity for a particular binding site.

papers.title: Rational Design of Novel Isosteviol-Derived Factor Xa Inhibitors Using Integrated QSAR, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA Analyses.
papers.abstract: Factor Xa (FXa) remains an important target in the development of anticoagulant and antithrombotic agents. In this study, twenty isosteviol-derived oxime ether analogs previously reported as FXa inhibitors were used to develop a predictive QSAR model. The compounds were geometry-optimized at the B3LYP/6-311++G(d,p) level, and Dragon molecular descriptors were calculated from the optimized structures. After descriptor filtering, Random Forest-based supervised preselection and correlation-based pruning were applied. Several models of increasing complexity were evaluated, including multiple linea
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods (QSAR, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and MM/GBSA) to rationally design novel isosteviol-derived inhibitors of Factor Xa, an anticoagulant target. The authors developed a predictive model from 20 known analogs and used it to guide the design of new potential inhibitors, providing a framework for structure-based drug discovery of antithrombotic agents.

papers.title: Higher-order assembly of a type IX retron enables exploitation for designer antimicrobials.
papers.abstract: Bacterial defense systems provide a rich reservoir for biotechnological innovation. Retrons are tripartite abortive infection systems that detect phage invasion using reverse-transcribed DNA (msDNA), but how they structurally couple threat detection to effector activation remains poorly understood. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structure and activation mechanism of retron-Kva2, a type IX retron from the human pathogen Klebsiella variicola. We reveal that retron-Kva2 assembles into an asymmetric, higher-order ribonucleoprotein complex that sequesters a toxic dimeric HEPN RNase at its core. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reveals the cryo-EM structure of a type IX retron from Klebsiella variicola, showing it assembles into a higher-order ribonucleoprotein complex that sequesters a toxic HEPN RNase dimer. The structural insights explain how threat detection is coupled to effector activation and enable the retron to be repurposed for designer antimicrobials.

papers.title: Drying-Induced Structural and Oxidative Transformations in Sustainable Proteins: Impact on Physicochemical Properties and Flavor-Binding Functionality.
papers.abstract: The rapid global transition toward sustainable food systems has intensified interest in alternative protein ingredients derived from both terrestrial plants and blue foods. However, a critical bottleneck in the commercialization of these proteins is the stabilization of flavor profiles during dehydration. Drying technologies ranging from conventional hot-air and heat pump drying to microwave and vacuum freeze-drying inevitably induce structural reorganization and oxidative modifications. These transformations fundamentally modulate how volatile flavor compounds are bound, retained, and release
papers.summary: This review examines how different drying methods (hot-air, heat pump, microwave, and vacuum freeze-drying) alter the structure and oxidation state of alternative proteins from plants and blue foods, and how these changes affect flavor compound binding and release. The authors highlight that drying-induced structural reorganization and oxidative modifications are critical bottlenecks for stabilizing flavor profiles in sustainable protein ingredients.

papers.title: Structure-Based Screening of Antiviral Candidates Against Infectious Spleen and Kidney Necrosis Virus (ISKNV) Using Molecular Docking and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Infectious spleen and kidney necrosis virus (ISKNV) causes systemic infections and high mortality in various freshwater and marine fish species, posing a serious threat to aquaculture and ornamental fish industries. In this study, 72 antiviral compounds were screened against five ISKNV target proteins, DNA polymerase, transcription elongation factor (TFIIS), adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase), ankyrin repeat-containing protein, and major capsid protein (MCP) using molecular docking, followed by in vitro evaluation in dwarf gourami fin (DGF) cells. Fludarabine, liquiritin, and lycorine consisten
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking to screen 72 antiviral compounds against five target proteins of infectious spleen and kidney necrosis virus (ISKNV), identifying fludarabine, liquiritin, and lycorine as promising candidates, which were then validated in vitro in dwarf gourami fin cells. The findings provide potential therapeutic leads against ISKNV, a significant threat to aquaculture.

papers.title: Targeting the RSV and hMPV L Protein: Cryo-EM and Structure-Based Approaches to Antiviral Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), members of the family Pneumoviridae, represent a foremost global cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection in infants, young children, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. Despite the recent approval of preventive vaccines and monoclonal antibody prophylactics targeting the viral fusion protein, no widely adopted, RSV-specific direct-acting antiviral is currently approved for routine post-infection treatment. The large (L) protein of the viral RNA polymerase complex, which catalyzes genome replication and mRN
papers.summary: This review discusses the RSV and hMPV L protein as a promising target for antiviral drug development, highlighting recent cryo-EM structures and structure-based approaches that could lead to direct-acting antivirals. It emphasizes the urgent need for post-infection treatments despite existing vaccines and prophylactics.

papers.title: Tryptophan Residues' Incorporation Modulates Ferritin Thermal Stability and Hydrophobicity.
papers.abstract: Ferritin, a physiological iron-storage protein, has emerged as a highly attractive platform for drug delivery owing to its biocompatibility, structural robustness, and intrinsic ability to encapsulate and protect therapeutic cargo within its hollow nanocage. Building upon previous studies that established the baseline characteristics of engineered ferritin mutants in comparison to the wild-type protein, this work specifically investigates and directly compares the thermal stability profiles of two distinct mutated variants. These variants of human H-chain ferritin, obtained through targeted si
papers.summary: This study investigates how incorporating tryptophan residues into human H-chain ferritin affects its thermal stability and surface hydrophobicity, comparing two engineered mutants against the wild-type protein. The findings reveal that tryptophan incorporation modulates these properties, which could inform the design of ferritin-based drug delivery vehicles with tailored stability and cargo-loading characteristics.

papers.title: Nanozymes in the Treatment of Pediatric Inflammatory Diseases: Opportunities and Challenges.
papers.abstract: Pediatric inflammatory diseases, such as neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and asthma, pose numerous challenges in clinical treatment due to their complex pathogenesis and the still-developing stage of children's immune systems. These challenges include poor precision, strong toxic and side effects, and unclear long-term biological safety. In recent years, the development of nanozymes has provided new opportunities to address these issues. This review systematically summarizes the latest research progress of nanozymes in the diagnosis and treatment
papers.summary: This review discusses the potential of nanozymes—nanomaterials with enzyme-like activity—for treating pediatric inflammatory diseases such as necrotizing enterocolitis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, and asthma. It highlights how nanozymes could offer improved precision and fewer side effects compared to conventional therapies, while also addressing challenges like long-term safety and clinical translation.

papers.title: Integrating Molecular Similarity and AlphaFold-Based Structural Alignment for Target Discovery in Trypanosoma cruzi.
papers.abstract: Background: Chagas disease, caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, remains a major neglected tropical disease, with millions of people living with the infection worldwide. Current treatments are effective in the acute stage of the disease, but are poorly tolerated and show reduced efficacy in chronic infections, highlighting an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. A key bottleneck in early-stage drug discovery is target identification, which is traditionally dependent on costly and low-throughput experimental methods. Computational approaches offer a cost-effective and fast alterna
papers.summary: This study presents a computational workflow that combines molecular similarity and AlphaFold-based structural alignment to identify potential drug targets in Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite causing Chagas disease. The approach offers a cost-effective alternative to experimental target identification, potentially accelerating early-stage drug discovery for this neglected tropical disease.

papers.title: Hierarchy of grammar rules for the language of transcriptional activation domains.
papers.abstract: Transcriptional activation domains (ADs) of eukaryotic gene activators have remained enigmatic for decades as short, consensus-less, extremely variable amino acid sequences that lack a specific structure and interact fuzzily with an uncertain number of targets. Understanding AD sequence grammar is critical for solving the enigma. Using rational design of AD sequences and high-throughput in vivo experimentation combined with bioinformatic analysis and machine learning, we refined grammar rules for AD sequences, calculated the relative importance of each rule to define a rule hierarchy, and link
papers.summary: This study refines the sequence grammar rules for transcriptional activation domains (ADs), which are short, unstructured, and highly variable sequences that activate gene expression. By combining rational design, high-throughput in vivo assays, bioinformatics, and machine learning, the authors establish a hierarchy of rules and their relative importance, providing a clearer framework for understanding and predicting AD function.

papers.title: Inhibition of amyloid β aggregation by venetoclax: a computational and in vitro experimental approach.
papers.abstract: The aggregation of amyloid β-protein (Aβ) plays a key role in the pathological progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Given the current absence of effective therapeutic strategies, the drug repurposing approach provides novel insights into the treatment of AD. Venetoclax, a B-cell lymphoma 2 (BCL-2) inhibitor, has demonstrated remarkable efficacy in the treatment of hematological malignancies, characterized by well-defined pharmacokinetic properties and a favorable safety profile. However, its effects and molecular mechanisms in the treatment of AD remain unexplored. Here, we investigated th
papers.summary: This study explores venetoclax, an existing cancer drug, as a potential treatment for Alzheimer's disease by computationally and experimentally testing its ability to inhibit amyloid beta aggregation. The findings suggest that venetoclax may reduce aggregation, offering a promising drug-repurposing avenue for AD therapy.

papers.title: Ziziphusine A, a unique plant-alkaloid featuring amide rotational isomerism from the fruits of Ziziphus jujuba with anti-inflammatory activity.
papers.abstract: Ziziphus jujuba var. inermis Rehder (Rhamnaceae) is an edible medicinal plant widely used in traditional medicine and functional foods. Phytochemical investigation of the methanolic extract of its fruits resulted in the isolation of a rare amide rotational isomeric alkaloid, ziziphusine A (1), together with eight known compounds including brassicasterol (2), (E)-24-nor-cholest-22-en-3β-ol (3), alphitolic acid (4), 3-O-cis-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (5), 3-O-trans-p-coumaroyl alphitolic acid (6), E-p-methoxycinnamic acid (7), (Z)-3-(4,5-dihydroxy-2-methoxyphenyl)acrylic acid (8), and scopoleti
papers.summary: This study reports the isolation and structural elucidation of ziziphusine A, a rare alkaloid with amide rotational isomerism, from the fruits of Ziziphus jujuba, along with eight known compounds. The compound shows anti-inflammatory activity, highlighting the potential of jujuba fruits as a source of bioactive natural products.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomics and single-cell analysis identify SIX4 as a candidate epithelial target in ovarian cancer and PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer is a heterogeneous solid tumor, whereas polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a distinct endocrine-metabolic ovarian disorder. Whether PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation and ovarian cancer share convergent transcriptomic candidates remains unclear. This study aimed to identify shared transcriptomic candidates and define their cellular localization without implying a causal or clinical comorbidity relationship.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify shared gene expression changes between ovarian cancer and PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation, pinpointing SIX4 as a candidate epithelial target. The findings suggest convergent molecular pathways in these distinct ovarian conditions, though the study does not imply a causal or clinical link between them.

papers.title: Integrative GC-MS, FT-IR, and Molecular Docking Analysis of Drimycarpus racemosus (Roxb.) Hook.f ex Marchand: In Vivo Analgesic and Antidiabetic Potential.
papers.abstract: Traditional medicine has long utilized Drimycarpus racemosus (Roxb.) Hook.f ex Marchand, which is a member of the Anacardiaceae family, to treat inflammation, pain, and metabolic disorders; however, its therapeutic properties have not been experimentally investigated. This study aimed to investigate the analgesic and hypoglycemic activities of D. racemosus leaf extract and explore its bioactive constituents through a computational approach. The most prevalent chemicals found in the plant methanolic extract, according to GC-MS analysis, were Furfural, 4-methoxybenzoic acid, methyl ester and β-s
papers.summary: This study experimentally validates the analgesic and antidiabetic potential of Drimycarpus racemosus leaf extract, supporting its traditional medicinal use. GC-MS and FT-IR identified key bioactive compounds, and molecular docking suggested plausible interactions with therapeutic targets, providing a preliminary basis for further drug development.

papers.title: In silico identification of selective cyclodecapeptide inhibitors targeting Plasmodium falciparum Grp78 chaperone.
papers.abstract: The increase in drug resistance by Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) remains a major challenge in eradicating malaria. The parasite drug resistance towards first line antimalarial therapy is associated with the parasite response to drug induced endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. The ER resident glucose-regulated protein 78 (PfGrp78) has been implicated as an ER stress response sensor. PfGrp78 binds to stressed protein substrates to suppress their misfolding and increase the capacity of the parasite ER to maintain proteostasis for parasite survival under stress. However, there have been limited effort
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify selective cyclodecapeptide inhibitors targeting the Plasmodium falciparum chaperone protein PfGrp78, which is involved in the parasite's stress response and drug resistance. The findings provide a promising starting point for developing novel antimalarial therapeutics that disrupt this protective mechanism.

papers.title: Valorization of Ficus carica Pruning Residues as Selective Botanical Insecticides: Optimized Furanocoumarin Extraction, Efficacy Against Neotropical Stink Bugs, and Mechanistic Insights via Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: The Neotropical stink bugs Euschistus heros and Diceraeus melacanthus are major pests of soybean and maize in South America, yet current chemical control strategies face widespread resistance, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable alternatives. This study investigates Ficus carica pruning residues as a source of selective botanical insecticides, integrating optimized extraction, phytochemical profiling, bioassays, and molecular modeling. Eight extracts were prepared under varying solvent, temperature, and acidity conditions, and analyzed for total phenolic content (TPC) and the key fura
papers.journal: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
papers.summary: This study explores the use of fig tree pruning waste as a source of natural insecticides against major soybean and maize pests in South America. The researchers optimized extraction methods for furanocoumarins, tested the extracts' effectiveness against stink bugs, and used molecular docking to understand how these compounds work, offering a sustainable alternative to chemical pesticides.

papers.title: Phytochemical Characterization of Echeveria "Blue Curls" and Its Association With Redox-Metabolic Perturbations in Melanoma Cells.
papers.abstract: Melanoma cells exhibit characteristic vulnerabilities in redox homeostasis and metabolic plasticity, making these processes attractive targets for natural-product-based intervention. In the present study, the aqueous extract of Echeveria "Blue Curls" (BCAE) was investigated through integrated phytochemical profiling, computational analysis, and cellular assays in B16-F10 melanoma cells. Untargeted GC-MS analysis tentatively identified eight putative metabolites, predominantly saccharides and organic acids, while molecular docking generated hypothetical binding models between selected constitue
papers.summary: This study characterizes the phytochemical composition of an aqueous extract from Echeveria 'Blue Curls' and explores its effects on redox and metabolic pathways in melanoma cells. Using GC-MS, they identified eight putative metabolites (mainly saccharides and organic acids) and used molecular docking to model potential interactions with cellular targets. The findings suggest this plant extract may perturb redox-metabolic homeostasis in melanoma cells, offering a potential natural-product-based intervention.

papers.title: Manufacturing and electrostatic surface optimization of CAR-T cells improve therapeutic efficacy in liver malignancies.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has achieved remarkable success in hematologic malignancies, yet demonstrates limited efficacy in solid tumors, including hepatic cancers. T-cell exhaustion and insufficient persistence represent major obstacles. We hypothesized that optimizing both manufacturing processes and CAR structural design could reduce exhaustion and enhance therapeutic outcomes in immunocompetent mouse models of primary and metastatic liver malignancies.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that optimizing CAR-T cell manufacturing and electrostatic surface properties improves their therapeutic efficacy against liver cancers in immunocompetent mouse models. The approach reduces T-cell exhaustion and enhances persistence, addressing key barriers to CAR-T therapy in solid tumors.

papers.title: RCSB protein data Bank: Next-generation advanced search for exploration of experimental structures and computed structure models.
papers.abstract: The Protein Data Bank (PDB), established in 1971, is the primary global, open-access archive for experimentally determined 3D macromolecular structures (proteins, RNA, DNA). The research-focused RCSB.org web-portal provides access to these data alongside more than one million machine-learning-predicted structure models, greatly expanding the available structural landscape. Rapid growth of both experimental and computational structures has increased the need for powerful yet accessible search tools that serve a broad and diverse scientific community. Herein, we describe a redesigned RCSB Protei
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: This paper describes a redesigned advanced search interface for the RCSB Protein Data Bank, which now integrates both experimental structures and over one million machine-learning-predicted structure models. The new search tools are designed to be powerful yet accessible, addressing the growing need for efficient exploration of the expanded structural landscape.

papers.title: FAERS-based pharmacovigilance and network toxicology analysis of esomeprazole-associated osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a progressive skeletal disorder often exacerbated by pharmacological agents. Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), particularly esomeprazole, have been epidemiologically linked to OP, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses FAERS pharmacovigilance data and network toxicology to investigate the association between esomeprazole (a proton pump inhibitor) and osteoporosis. It confirms a significant signal for esomeprazole-associated osteoporosis and identifies potential molecular mechanisms through network analysis, providing new insights into this drug safety concern.

papers.title: The Redesign of the Molecular Scaffold of Viral Ion Channel Blockers.
papers.abstract: The rise of rapidly mutating viruses poses growing challenges for drug developers in the fight against antiviral resistance. Viral ion channels generally have low mutation rates and are therefore considered emerging targets for a sustainable solution to the problem of resistance. This study reports the redesign of scaffolds for drug candidates targeting viral ion channels. The redesign was powered by a combination of a computational docking protocol that accounts for water molecules (HydroDock) and a subsequent quantum mechanics-based scoring (QMH-L) of the drug candidates. Extending the antiv
papers.summary: This study reports the redesign of drug candidate scaffolds targeting viral ion channels, which are attractive antiviral targets due to their low mutation rates. The redesign uses a computational docking protocol (HydroDock) combined with quantum mechanics-based scoring (QMH-L) to optimize the candidates.

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 NSP8-Derived Peptide Effectively Suppresses the Activity of Helicase NSP13.
papers.abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) nonstructural protein 13 (NSP13) is a multifunctional helicase that plays a central role in viral RNA replication and suppression of host innate immunity. Beyond its essential function within the replication-transcription complex (RTC), NSP13 antagonizes type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling through interaction with the host kinase TBK1, making its protein-protein interactions attractive antiviral targets. In this study, we investigated whether fragments derived from the viral cofactor NSP8 can competitively interfere with NSP13 intera
papers.summary: This study identifies a peptide derived from SARS-CoV-2 NSP8 that can suppress the helicase activity of NSP13, a key viral protein involved in RNA replication and immune evasion. The peptide likely acts by competitively disrupting NSP13's interactions, offering a potential new antiviral strategy against COVID-19.

papers.title: Integrating machine learning, deep learning, and docking to predict aristolochic acid A carcinogenesis.
papers.abstract: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms of renal clear cell carcinoma (RCC) induced by Aristolochic acid A (AAA) using machine learning, deep learning, and molecular docking approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning, deep learning, and molecular docking to investigate how aristolochic acid A (AAA) may cause renal clear cell carcinoma. It identifies potential molecular mechanisms and targets, providing a computational framework for predicting AAA carcinogenesis.

papers.title: CCR1-mediated monocyte chemotaxis in the immunopathology of primary Sjögren's syndrome: multi-omics integration analysis and computational target prioritization implicating Polygonatum odoratum.
papers.abstract: Primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease with no specific etiological treatment. Polygonatum odoratum, a traditional yin-nourishing herb, is used in treating pSS, but its molecular mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the potential association of CCR1 with pSS immunopathology and to computationally assess its candidacy as a predicted target of P. odoratum.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics integration and computational analysis to identify CCR1-mediated monocyte chemotaxis as a key pathway in primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) immunopathology, and computationally predicts that the herb Polygonatum odoratum may target CCR1. The findings provide a potential molecular mechanism for the herb's therapeutic effect and suggest CCR1 as a candidate drug target for pSS.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular modelling analysis of Arctium lappa phytochemicals in valproic acid-induced hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Valproic acid (VPA) is an antiepileptic drug commonly employed to treat epilepsy. Despite this, the clinical application of VPA is often hindered by adverse reactions. This study aims to investigate the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals obtained from Arctium lappa to mitigate VPA-induced toxicity and to determine the mechanisms involved.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular modeling to investigate whether phytochemicals from Arctium lappa (greater burdock) can counteract liver and pancreas toxicity caused by the antiepileptic drug valproic acid. The authors identify key compounds and their potential protein targets, suggesting a mechanistic basis for the protective effects of these natural products.

papers.title: Integrative Multiomics Analysis Reveals a Cancer Stem Cell-Driven Prognostic Signature and Nominates Belinostat for Targeted Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) suffers from a poor prognosis largely due to its profound molecular heterogeneity and high frequency of relapse, challenges that are closely linked to the biology of cancer stem cells (CSCs) and a lack of effective stemness-related prognostic biomarkers. Identifying CSC-related prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets is critical for improving patient outcomes.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multiomics analysis to identify a cancer stem cell-driven prognostic signature in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), which could improve patient risk stratification. The authors also nominate the drug belinostat as a potential targeted therapy for HCC based on this signature.

papers.title: Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre leaf extract: in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches to combat the waterborne bacterial pathogens associated with diarrheal conditions.
papers.abstract: Pongamia pinnata (L.) Pierre, a medicinal plant traditionally used in Indian ethnomedicine, was evaluated for its antidiarrheal, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties through a combination of in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. This study aims to study the traditional use of plants in medicine and identify a suitable secondary metabolite that can help reduce bacterial growth in living systems, thereby lowering the risk of waterborne diseases and diarrhea. Screening of P. pinnata leaf extract confirmed the presence of various bioactive classes, including alkaloids, flavonoids, etc.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates the medicinal plant Pongamia pinnata for its antidiarrheal, antibacterial, and antioxidant properties using in vitro, in vivo, and in silico methods. The leaf extract contains bioactive compounds like alkaloids and flavonoids that may help combat waterborne bacterial pathogens associated with diarrhea, supporting its traditional use.

papers.title: An NRIP1-Centric Monocyte Immunogenetic Bridge Between Heart Failure and Ischemic Stroke.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF) and ischemic stroke (IS) frequently co-occur and worsen each other. Circulating immune cells may act as a cross-organ inflammatory bridge, but the key immune lineage, genetically supported mediators, and druggable targets remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study identifies a monocyte-centered immunogenetic link between heart failure and ischemic stroke, highlighting NRIP1 as a key mediator and potential druggable target. The findings suggest that specific immune cell populations and genetic pathways may serve as a bridge connecting these two conditions.

papers.title: PTM-Related Signatures Predict Lymph Node Metastasis and Shape Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Single-Cell and Bulk Integrated Analysis.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has a poor prognosis with lymph node metastasis (LNM), severely impacting survival. Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate tumor microenvironment (TME) dynamics, but their role in HCC LNM is unknown.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify post-translational modification (PTM)-related gene signatures that predict lymph node metastasis (LNM) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The authors show that these PTM signatures are associated with the tumor microenvironment, potentially offering a prognostic tool and insights into the mechanisms of LNM in HCC.

papers.title: In-silico characterization of PSEN1 missense variants associated with acne inversa.
papers.abstract: Acne inversa, or hidradenitis suppurativa, is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder that causes painful and reoccurring abscesses. The PSEN1 gene is responsible for the sequence coding for the presenilin 1 protein, which is part of the gamma-secretase complex and is responsible for cleaving multiple peptides. Acne inversa occurs when the Notch signaling pathway of PSEN1 is disrupted. Analysis of multiple pathogenicity predictors and simulated aqueous environments of the transmembrane protein in its native state and mutated state through molecular dynamics simulation predicted deleterious effect
papers.summary: This study computationally characterized PSEN1 missense variants associated with acne inversa, using pathogenicity predictors and molecular dynamics simulations to assess their effects on the transmembrane protein. The analysis predicted that these mutations are likely deleterious, disrupting the Notch signaling pathway and contributing to disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: Pharmacologic targeting of midasin (MDN1) reveals a potential therapeutic vulnerability in ESR1-mutant breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Although most cases of estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer initially respond to endocrine therapy, many patients ultimately develop resistance. A major contributor to endocrine resistance in metastatic disease is the acquisition of constitutively active somatic mutations in the estrogen receptor ligand-binding domain (LBD). We previously identified midasin (MDN1), a ribosome biogenesis protein, as significantly overexpressed in letrozole-resistant MCF-7 cells. Because these cells are ERlow/- and represent only a subset of endocrine-resistant tumors, we hypothesized that ESR1 mutatio
papers.summary: This study identifies midasin (MDN1), a ribosome biogenesis protein, as a potential therapeutic target in ESR1-mutant breast cancer, which is a major cause of endocrine therapy resistance. The authors demonstrate that pharmacologic targeting of MDN1 may exploit a vulnerability in these resistant tumors, offering a new treatment strategy.

papers.title: Elucidating the molecular mechanisms of paeoniflorin intervention in oral lichen planus: a computational biology and bioinformatics-based research strategy.
papers.abstract: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory mucosal disease with a risk of malignant transformation and limited long-term therapeutic options. Paeoniflorin (PF), a natural monoterpene glycoside, exhibits multi-target anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties, but its systematic mechanisms against OLP remain elusive.
papers.summary: This study uses computational biology and bioinformatics approaches to investigate how paeoniflorin, a natural compound, may treat oral lichen planus by targeting multiple inflammatory and immune pathways. The findings provide a systematic molecular mechanism for paeoniflorin's therapeutic effects, potentially guiding future drug development for this chronic mucosal disease.

papers.title: Integrative network pharmacology, transcriptomics, and molecular docking identify candidate Centella asiatica constituents and targets in neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and Huntington's disease (HD), are progressive disorders with limited therapeutic options. Centella asiatica (C. asiatica), a medicinal and edible plant, has been reported to exert neuroprotective and anti-neuroinflammatory properties. Yet, the mechanisms underlying its effects against neurodegenerative diseases remain largely unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, transcriptomics, and molecular docking to identify candidate bioactive constituents of Centella asiatica and their potential molecular targets in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and Huntington's diseases. The findings reveal key compounds and pathways that may underlie the plant's neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects, offering a mechanistic basis for its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Rhizosphere microecological characteristics associated with tobacco root-knot nematode disease.
papers.abstract: Root-knot nematode disease poses a serious threat to the production of tobacco and other crops, but the rhizosphere microecological response mechanisms during disease development remain unclear. In this study, we collected rhizosphere soil from healthy and diseased tobacco plants in typical tobacco-growing areas of Kunming, Yunnan Province, China, and we systematically identified the differences in soil physicochemical properties, enzyme activities, and the microbial community composition and structure based on 16S rDNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. Compared to healthy rhizosphere soil, disease
papers.summary: This study characterizes the rhizosphere microbiome of tobacco plants affected by root-knot nematode disease, comparing healthy and diseased soils using 16S rDNA and ITS amplicon sequencing. The findings reveal distinct shifts in microbial community composition and structure, along with changes in soil physicochemical properties and enzyme activities, providing insights into the microecological mechanisms associated with disease development.

papers.title: Bacteriophage lysins: a promising strategy for combating foodborne pathogens in food safety.
papers.abstract: Food safety is a major public concern, with foodborne pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus, Listeria monocytogenes, Clostridium perfringens, and Vibrio parahaemolyticus causing millions of infections and significant economic losses annually. Phage and endolysin therapies have emerged as promising environmentally friendly strategies for pathogen control. Bacteriophage lytic enzymes, which are proteins produced during the late stage of phage infection, offer advantages over whole phages, including rapid bactericidal action, a broad antibacterial spectrum, and a low risk of inducing resistance
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of bacteriophage lysins (endolysins) as a promising strategy to combat foodborne pathogens in food safety. It highlights their advantages over whole phages, including rapid bactericidal action, broad spectrum, and low resistance risk, positioning them as an environmentally friendly alternative for controlling pathogens like Staphylococcus aureus and Listeria monocytogenes.

papers.title: Licensed and investigational TLR4 agonists as vaccine adjuvants: structural basis, clinical progress, and future directions.
papers.abstract: The development of innovative vaccine platforms, including protein subunit and nucleic acid vaccines, has advanced rapidly and established new technical paradigms for infectious disease prophylaxis. Nonetheless, many next-generation vaccines display suboptimal intrinsic immunogenicity owing to restricted antigenic complexity, resulting in inadequate protective immunity when delivered without adjuvants. Aluminum-containing adjuvants, the most widely deployed clinical adjuvants, primarily potentiate humoral immunity but elicit modest cellular immune responses, thereby failing to satisfy the immu
papers.summary: This review examines licensed and investigational TLR4 agonists as vaccine adjuvants, detailing their structural basis, clinical progress, and future directions. It highlights how these agonists can enhance both humoral and cellular immunity, addressing limitations of aluminum-based adjuvants in next-generation vaccines.

papers.title: Theta-Defensin Proteins: Conformational Variability and Environmental Effects.
papers.abstract: Theta-defensins are a unique class of cyclic antimicrobial peptides known for their exceptional structural stability and broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity. Despite their therapeutic potential in mammals, the effects of solvent environments and specific mutations on their conformational stability remain poorly understood. This paper employs all-atom molecular dynamics simulations under different solvent conditions to investigate the structural dynamics of baboon theta-defensin-2 (BTD-2) peptides, as well as solvent effects. BTD-2 was selected due to its higher arginine content, enhancing it
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to explore how different solvent environments and specific mutations affect the conformational stability of baboon theta-defensin-2 (BTD-2), a cyclic antimicrobial peptide. The findings reveal that solvent conditions and arginine content significantly influence the peptide's structural dynamics, providing insights that could inform the design of more stable therapeutic peptides.
